name: משיק לגרף פונקציה בנקודה – עם גרף אינטראקטיבי (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Consider the function \({\displaystyle f(x) = {{CT:0}}}\) whose graph is displayed below.

The tangent line through the point \(P=({{CT:1}}, {{CT:2}})\) is also a function. Determine its expression.

You can use the graph below: move the points A and B along the curve. As they approach the point P, the secant line AB approaches the tangent line; the slope of AB is shown at the top of the graph. There are other ways to solve this problem.

[[jsxgraph width="100%" aspect-ratio="1.3"]] var A3 = {{CT:3}}, B2 = {{CT:4}}, C1 = {{CT:5}}, D0 = {{CT:6}}; var x0 = {{CT:7}}, y0 = {{CT:8}}; var f = function (x) { return ((A3*x + B2)*x + C1)*x + D0; }; var xl = x0 - 2, xr = x0 + 2, ymin = Math.min(y0, 0), ymax = Math.max(y0, 0); for (var i = 0; i <= 200; i++) { var v = f(xl + (xr - xl)*i/200); if (v < ymin) ymin = v; if (v > ymax) ymax = v; } var pad = 0.12*(ymax - ymin) + 0.5, left = Math.min(xl, -0.5); var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [left, ymax + pad, xr, ymin - pad], axis: true, keepaspectratio: false, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false} }); var G = board.create('functiongraph', [f, xl, xr], {strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: '#1f5fa8', fixed: true}); board.create('point', [x0, y0], {name: 'P', fixed: true, size: 3, color: '#222', label: {offset: [-14, 12]}}); var A = board.create('glider', [x0 - 1.5, f(x0 - 1.5), G], {name: 'A', size: 4, color: '#4b1f6f'}); var B = board.create('glider', [x0 + 1.5, f(x0 + 1.5), G], {name: 'B', size: 4, color: '#4b1f6f'}); board.create('line', [A, B], {strokeColor: '#4b1f6f', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 2}); board.create('text', [left + 0.55*(xr - left), ymax + 0.6*pad, function () { var dx = B.X() - A.X(); return Math.abs(dx) < 1e-9 ? 'slope(AB) = ?' : 'slope(AB) = ' + ((B.Y() - A.Y())/dx).toFixed(3); }], {fixed: true, fontSize: 15}); [[/jsxgraph]]

generalfeedback:
Outline: The slope of the tangent line is the derivative at the point of tangency; the point-slope form of the line then gives its \(y\)-intercept and its expression.
Step 1 — The slope (part a)
The point \(P=({{CT:1}}, {{CT:2}})\) lies on the graph: \(f({{CT:1}})={{CT:2}}\). The slope of the tangent line at \(P\) is the value of the derivative there. Differentiating term by term,

\[ f'(x)={{CT:9}}, \qquad k=f'({{CT:1}})={{CT:10}}. \]

Step 2 — The \(y\)-intercept (part b)
The tangent line passes through \(P\) with slope \(k\): \(y-{{CT:2}}={{CT:10}}\left(x-{{CT:1}}\right)\). Setting \(x=0\), it crosses the \(y\)-axis at

\[ b={{CT:2}}-\left({{CT:10}}\right)\cdot {{CT:1}}={{CT:11}}. \]

Step 3 — The tangent line (part c)
Hence the tangent line is

\[ g(x)={{CT:12}}. \]
